name: Restart and catch-up.
line: A stopped isolate starts again and catches up from the bus.
text: The kernel expects a heartbeat from every loop. After 400 ms without one, an isolate is marked blocked. After `killAfterMs` (10 s by default; basic uses 2 s) its worker is stopped and started again. Three restarts within a minute and it’s marked failed, and stays down: that’s the crash-loop guard, so an isolate that keeps crashing stops costing restarts. `kernel.restart(id)` brings it back.

Restarted, each subscription starts where its `from` says, except in a consumer group that has committed, which resumes after its commit. `committed` reads on after its last commit; commits go out every 100 ms, so the few records it had read but not committed come again: at least once, none lost. `earliest` reads everything the topic still retains. `latest`, the default, starts with new records.

proof.test: a member stopped right after a redelivery loses nothing
I3 and I1: four crashes fail C; A, B and D stay running, responsive and untouched
